Google has done this exact same thing to help aggregate data for many of its applications. Over a decade ago they used to have a game that would match you with a random person (or bot) online, show you both the same image, then you would have 60 seconds to enter as many tags as you could for the image (e.g. "green", "tree", "park"...). You got points based on how many similar matches you and your partner had. They used that data to help the relevance of the early Google Image Search results.

They have done several similar things with bike paths, walking paths, geo caching, GPS location services for store/business locations and information, etc.

It's somewhat similar to Amazon's Mechanical Turk - using a distributed force of humans to aggregate big data. The only difference is that you get paid for participating on Mechanical Turk.

Google's ReCAPTCHA has been crowdsourcing work for years. Their text-based CAPTCHAs help with processing and/or proofreading their Google Books OCR project, and their house-number-based CAPTCHAs help with identifying house numbers for Google Street View. You're earning Google a little money while you prove your humanity. The latter is necessary, so your effort might as well not go to waste.
